title: Why Is Fortinet Stock Falling, and is it a Buying Opportunity? | FTNT Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc revisits Fortinet after its post-earnings crash, asking whether the dip is a buying opportunity. The quarter itself was strong: billings grew 29% and revenue 20%, with billings ahead of revenue growth, which he reads as a sign that growth is sustainable and possibly accelerating. The company also raised its forecast for the third time in 2026, delivered record 33% trailing operating margins (up from around 4% in 2017) and a 111% return on invested capital, which he calls among the best of any company he follows. Yet the shares fell, which he attributes to a price that had already run up triple digits on agentic-AI cybersecurity enthusiasm; he had downgraded Fortinet from BUY to HOLD a couple of months earlier for exactly that reason. Analysts have since cut expected EPS growth to 15.7% from 17%. With the forward price-to-earnings ratio down from over 50 to 35, his updated discounted cash flow value is $102 against a market price of about $100, so after a margin of safety the stock still looks slightly overvalued. Call: FTNT — HOLD (reiterated, not upgraded). Bull case: the agentic-AI cybersecurity boom with accelerating growth and expanding margins. Bear case: still slightly overvalued, with analyst growth estimates being revised down.
